subject: Maintenance carveout and proposed credit bands for monthly service availability
messages:
From: Claire Ortiz <claire.ortiz@wavepay.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@wavepay.io
Date: 2026-12-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: WavePay maintenance windows & SLA carveout request

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. As we prepare our procurement ask, a few things came up on the ops side that will affect how we evaluate the availability guarantee. WavePay runs a recurring maintenance cadence for database and billing runs that we can't shift entirely off peak. Rough summary:~

- Monthly scheduled maintenance: up to 8 hours (usually a 2x4h window)
- Quarterly larger maintenance: up to 16 hours (planned 30–60d in advance)

Two asks from our side: 1) Can scheduled maintenance be carved out from uptime calculations if windows are scheduled ahead of time and 2) can you propose a monthly credit schedule that recognizes scheduled maintenance rather than treating it as unplanned downtime?

I've attached our maintenance calendar and an initial list of SLA items we need to see. For context, the finance team will count any availability credit against our committed spend, so clarity on caps and calculation is important.

Attachments: wavepay_expected_maintenance_calendar_2027.csv, wavepay_initial_sla_requests.docx

Happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

Best,
Claire Ortiz
Head of Ops, WavePay, Inc.
claire.ortiz@wavepay.io
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ortiz <claire.ortiz@wavepay.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T12:40:00Z
Subject: Re: WavePay maintenance windows & SLA carveout request

Hi Claire,

Really appreciate the detail — this helps. We can accommodate a maintenance carveout with a few guardrails so it can't be used to mask service issues:

1) Scheduled maintenance: up to 8 hours per calendar month (two 4h windows) will be excluded from availability calculations if windows are: scheduled at least 72 hours in advance, documented in a shared maintenance calendar, and communicated to support@redwood.com.

2) Quarterly larger events: up to 16 hours per quarter if scheduled 30+ days in advance and added to the same shared calendar.

3) Emergency maintenance: will not be excluded unless we can demonstrate (logs + RCA) that the action was required to prevent an ongoing incident.

Proposed monthly credit bands (post-carveout calculation):
- Monthly availability >= 99.90%: no credit
- >= 99.50% and < 99.90%: 5% credit of that month’s recurring fee
- >= 99.00% and < 99.50%: 20% credit
- < 99.00%: 40% credit

We generally cap credits at 25% for Dedicated customers, but since WavePay has specific maintenance needs I want to discuss whether we offer the full table above or set a cap (our standard approach is to cap credits at 100% of the monthly recurring charges for extreme outages).

Looping in Marissa (legal) and Ben (sales) to weigh in on caps and contract language. If this looks directionally right, I'll draft an SLA addendum for your review and include the maintenance calendar as an exhibit.

Thanks,
Sean
Director, Commercial 
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-11T14:00:00Z
Subject: Fwd: WavePay maintenance windows & SLA carveout request

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Claire's ask and my proposed bands. Key negotiation points:

- Carveout eligibility (72h vs 7 days advance)
- Monthly vs quarterly carveouts and how to represent them in the calculation example
- Credit cap: WavePay wants clarity; finance may prefer a hard cap at 25% of MRR rather than open-ended percentages
- Whether we require WavePay to opt into a \"maintenance SLA\" (i.e., they accept scheduled windows and acknowledge carveouts in the contract)

I recommend Marissa propose conservative legal language (calendar exhibit, notice windows, emergency RCAs) and Ben can propose commercial limits. I can incorporate both into the addendum draft.

On a related note, for Dedicated customers we sometimes exclude planned maintenance performed by the customer (on-prem cases) entirely from Redwood liability — we should call that out for WavePay if they're considering private deployment.

--Sean
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: WavePay maintenance windows & SLA carveout request

Sean / Ben — my thoughts from a legal perspective:

1) Carveout mechanics: define two categories (routine scheduled maintenance and major scheduled maintenance). Routine = up to 8 hours/month with 72h notice and calendar listing; Major = up to 16 hours/quarter with 30d notice. Both excluded from availability if WavePay acknowledges the scheduled window via a simple reply email to support@redwood.com (we should keep the acknowledgement process light).

2) Emergency maintenance: allow carveout only if Redwood produces contemporaneous logs and an RCA within 7 business days demonstrating the emergency nature.

3) Credit cap: propose changing the open percentages to a single cap of 25% of the monthly recurring fee for any given month, but maintain the tiered credit table for clarity. This avoids unlimited exposure while preserving predictable remediation for WavePay.

4) Addendum: include exhibit A = monthly maintenance calendar (customer-provided) and exhibit B = sample calculation example for a hypothetical month (showing pre- and post-carveout availability math).

5) Private/Dedicated nuance: if WavePay opts for Private deployment, carveouts for customer-applied maintenance should be explicit and we should exclude Redwood liability for maintenance performed solely by the customer.

I'll draft redlines on the addendum and share. If we want to be more commercial, Ben can propose a smaller cap (15%) or a blended cap model.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ortiz <claire.ortiz@wavepay.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T16:47:00Z
Subject: Revised: Maintenance carveout proposal & next steps

Claire — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Attached is a draft addendum that reflects the changes Marissa suggested (summary below). Please review and confirm whether WavePay can accept this approach so we can finalize commercial terms.

Summary of the proposed approach (high level):
- Routine scheduled maintenance: up to 8 hours/month excluded (2x4h), 72 hours notice + calendar entry + simple email acknowledgement from WavePay
- Major scheduled maintenance: up to 16 hours/quarter excluded with 30 days notice and calendar entry
- Emergency maintenance: excluded only with logs + RCA within 7 business days
- Credit table (applied after carveouts): >=99.90% no credit; >=99.50% & <99.90% = 5% credit; >=99.00% & <99.50% = 20%; <99.00% = 40%
- Credit cap: 25% of that month’s recurring fee (applies to all calculations)
- Dedicated/private deployments: explicit carveout language for customer-driven maintenance; Redwood liability limited per addendum

Next steps:
1) If this is acceptable, please reply with a confirmation line (e.g., \"WavePay accepts the maintenance carveout addendum as drafted\") so we have a written acceptance for procurement.
2) We'll upload the addendum to HubSpot and send a DocuSign envelope (link below).
3) Once signed, Ben will follow up on PO/commit timing and billing details.
